user.title: Microsoft Family Safety
user.description: Configure the integration. After Submit, Home Assistant opens the Microsoft sign-in through a temporary authentication proxy. Sign in with the parent account and answer **Yes** to "Stay signed in?": that is what keeps the Family session valid for about a year instead of a few hours. If Home Assistant is not reachable over HTTPS, local HTTP can be explicitly enabled for testing; Microsoft credentials are then not transport-encrypted on the local network.

data_description.platforms: Windows, Mobile: one lock switch per ticked platform. The Xbox lock is not chosen here: it comes with Sign in to Xbox Family Settings and the xapprove option below, and the Xbox daily limits are always there. Nothing here needs the Microsoft web session.
data_description.allowed_users: Leave empty to let every user use the buttons and settings (default). As soon as users are ticked, only they and the administrators can: a child's non-administrator account is refused on every button, switch, limit and time window, and on the microsoft_family_safety actions. Automations and scripts run by Home Assistant are not affected. Give the child a non-administrator account: an administrator can change this option.
data_description.strict_mode: Off by default. When on, a Windows or Xbox lock placed by microsoft_family_safety.lock_platform that Microsoft reports as cancelled (for example from the Family Safety app) while it should still hold is placed again on the next update, at most every 10 minutes, and the event microsoft_family_safety_lock_reasserted is fired. unlock_platform ends it. Keep strict mode off when another integration (Hearth, for example) manages these locks: strict mode would place a lock again after a parent released it in the Family Safety app, fighting the parent's decision.
data_description.app_usage_sensors: 0 (default) = off. Otherwise each child's most used apps today, up to this number, get a sensor with their minutes used today, and the event microsoft_family_safety_app_usage fires when an app's usage grows between two updates. An app keeps its sensor once it has one.
data_description.xbox_xapprove: Off by default. Easiest: tick Sign in to Xbox Family Settings below; after the sign-in, Home Assistant checks it and offers to turn this on. When on (with that sign-in), the Xbox lock, unlock, the Xbox lock switch and Xbox extra time go through the Xbox Family Settings API; when that cannot be used, an Xbox lock falls back to today's Xbox schedule. A parent's own pause or extra time is never replaced. The Xbox never uses the Microsoft web session. The lock switch shows lock_path: xapprove or mobile_schedule.
data_description.xbox_xuids: Leave empty: each child's Xbox user id is looked up in your Xbox family. Only when that lookup fails (probe_xapprove says so), enter child=xuid pairs separated by commas, the child given by first name or account id, for example Alex=2533274800000000.
data_description.xbox_sign_in: Tick and submit to go to the sign-in page. The Xbox lock switch, the Xbox Override sensor and Xbox extra time need it. Use the same parent Microsoft account as for Family Safety. Tick it again to replace an earlier or expired sign-in. Unofficial use of the Xbox Family Settings app's sign-in: Microsoft can break or block it, and the Xbox lock then falls back to today's Xbox schedule. See the README.
data_description.xbox_sign_out: Tick and submit to forget the Xbox Family Settings sign-in (its refresh token and key). The Xbox lock then works the way it did before the sign-in.
data_description.xbox_sign_in_app: Try this when the sign-in above works but Xbox still refuses (probe_xapprove: every way 401). It signs in the way the Xbox Family Settings app does, with a computer's browser tools, and replaces the earlier Xbox sign-in while keeping its device key.

xbox_signin.title: Sign in to Xbox Family Settings
xbox_signin.description:
{why}Use the **parent** Microsoft account: the same one you sign in to Family Safety with, not a child's. This way needs a **computer** with Chrome, Edge or Firefox: the page you end on erases its own address (it becomes ...oauth20_desktop.srf?removed=true as soon as it has loaded), so the address has to be copied from the browser's network log, not from the address bar.

1. Open a new private or incognito window and press **F12** to open the developer tools. Go to the **Network** tab and tick **Preserve log**.
2. In that window, open [this sign-in link]({url}) (right-click it, Copy link address, and paste it into the window).
3. Sign in with the parent account and accept if Microsoft asks for permission. You end on a blank page.
4. In the Network tab, find the request named **oauth20_desktop.srf** (type it in the filter box). Right-click it and choose **Copy > Copy URL**. It starts with https://login.live.com/oauth20_desktop.srf?code= .
5. Paste it below and submit within a few minutes: the code in it expires soon.

Closed this page by mistake? Open Configure and tick the sign-in again within 10 minutes: the same link, and an address you already copied, still work.

data_description.redirect_url: Copied from the Network tab (Copy URL), starting with https://login.live.com/oauth20_desktop.srf?code= . Spaces or quotes around it do no harm.

xbox_signin_app.title: Sign in to Xbox Family Settings (app-style)
xbox_signin_app.description:
This signs in the way the Xbox Family Settings app does, which may be what Xbox needs before it lets Home Assistant pause the Xbox. Use the **parent** Microsoft account. Home Assistant opens the Microsoft sign-in in your browser and reads the result itself, so you do not need any developer tools. It keeps this entry's device key and replaces its refresh token.

Submit to open the sign-in. If your Home Assistant has no HTTPS address a browser can reach, tick **Paste the address myself instead** to use the manual way (a computer's browser tools).

data.paste_instead: Paste the address myself instead (no browser sign-in)

xbox_signin_app_paste.title: Sign in to Xbox Family Settings (app-style, paste)
xbox_signin_app_paste.description:
{why}This sign-in goes the way the Xbox Family Settings app does it, which may be what Xbox needs before it lets Home Assistant pause the Xbox. It keeps this entry's device key. Use the **parent** Microsoft account. Like the pasted-address sign-in, it needs a **computer** with Chrome, Edge or Firefox: the page you end on erases its own address, so the address is copied from the browser's network log.

1. Open a new private or incognito window and press **F12**. Go to the **Network** tab and tick **Preserve log**.
2. In that window, open [this sign-in link]({url}) (right-click it, Copy link address, paste it into the window).
3. Sign in with the parent account and accept if Microsoft asks. You end on a blank page.
4. In the Network tab, type **oauth20_desktop.srf** in the filter box, right-click the request and choose **Copy > Copy URL**. It starts with https://login.live.com/oauth20_desktop.srf?code= .
5. Paste it below and submit right away: the code and this sign-in expire within minutes.

Home Assistant then finishes the Xbox sign-in, reads your Xbox account the way the app's setup page does (it never creates or changes anything), and checks a child's Xbox settings. If you close this page, start again from Configure: the link is only good for this page.

data_description.redirect_url: Copied from the Network tab (Copy URL), starting with https://login.live.com/oauth20_desktop.srf?code= .

xbox_signin_works.title: Xbox control works
xbox_signin_works.description:
Signed in. Home Assistant read a child's Xbox settings with this sign-in, so it can pause the Xbox and give extra time through the Xbox Family Settings API.

Leave the box ticked and submit to use it. If it stops working later, the Xbox lock falls back to today's Xbox schedule and a Repairs issue says so.{finish}

data.xbox_xapprove: Use the Xbox Family Settings API for the Xbox lock and extra time

xbox_signin_refused.title: Xbox refused this sign-in
xbox_signin_refused.description:
The sign-in was saved, but Xbox refused to show a child's Xbox settings with it ({reason}). Meanwhile an Xbox lock goes through today's Xbox schedule.

Leave the box unticked and submit. Check that you signed in with the **parent** account; if not, open Configure and tick Sign in to Xbox Family Settings again. For details, run the action microsoft_family_safety.probe_xapprove.{finish}

xbox_signin_unchecked.title: Signed in, not checked yet

If no child was found in your Xbox family, check that you signed in with the parent account, or enter the Xbox user ids in Configure.{finish}

error.invalid_redirect: That is not the address of the sign-in's last page. Copy the oauth20_desktop.srf request's URL from the Network tab; it starts with https://login.live.com/oauth20_desktop.srf?code= .
error.state_mismatch: That address comes from an older sign-in link. Open the link on this page, sign in, and paste the new address.
error.signin_error: Microsoft stopped the sign-in ({detail}), for example because the permission was declined. Open the link again, sign in with the parent account and accept.
error.xbox_signin_failed: Signing in to Xbox Live did not work ({detail}). Nothing was saved and the Xbox lock keeps working the way it did. Try again in a few minutes; if it keeps failing, Microsoft may have blocked this sign-in (see the README).
error.pasted_link: That is the sign-in link itself. Open it, sign in, and paste the address of the blank page you land on afterwards.
error.code_expired: Microsoft no longer accepts that code: it expired, was already used, or was cut off when copying. Open the link again (it is quick when the account is still signed in) and paste the new address right away.
error.removed_address: That is the address after the page erased it (?removed=true): the code is no longer in it. Copy the address from the browser's Network tab instead: press F12, tick Preserve log, sign in with the link again, then right-click the oauth20_desktop.srf request and choose Copy > Copy URL.

lock_platform.name: Lock Platform
lock_platform.description: Lock a platform (Windows/Xbox/Mobile) for a child account until a time. The first lock saves the override Microsoft had in force (a parent's own lock, or none) so unlock_platform can put it back; a lock already in force that ends later is kept. Answers with the saved prior state, the lock applied and lock_path: web (Windows), xapprove (the Xbox through the Xbox Family Settings API; a parent's own pause or extra time is left alone: left_parent_override), or mobile_schedule (an Xbox lock placed through today's Xbox schedule when xapprove cannot be used, which ends at midnight at the latest). Keep strict mode off when another integration (Hearth, for example) manages these locks: strict mode would place a lock again after a parent released it in the Family Safety app, fighting the parent's decision.

duration_hours.description: Duration of the lock in hours (default 24). Give this or until, not both.

until.description: When the lock ends, instead of duration_hours. A time without an offset is Home Assistant's local time.

unlock_platform.name: Unlock Platform
unlock_platform.description: Unlock a platform (Windows/Xbox/Mobile) for a child account. Windows: puts back the lock that was in force before lock_platform if it has not run out yet, otherwise cancels the lock. Xbox: cancels only our own lock (lock_path xapprove), or puts the saved day back for a lock placed through today's Xbox schedule (lock_path mobile_schedule); a parent's change since is left alone (left_parent_override). Answers with the prior state, what was applied and lock_path. Keep strict mode off when another integration (Hearth, for example) manages these locks: strict mode would place a lock again after a parent released it in the Family Safety app, fighting the parent's decision.

sync_site_list.name: Sync Site List
sync_site_list.description: Keep the child's blocked websites in step with a published list of domains (one per line, '#' comments). Adds what the list gained and removes only what this same list added before and has since dropped; sites blocked by hand and allowed sites are left alone, and a domain sharing a site with an allowed one is skipped. The list must be served over https (redirects are not followed), is read up to 1 MiB, and only plain domains are taken. An empty or failed download, or one that would remove most of what the list added, changes nothing; stop removes everything the list added. Answers with what was added, removed, kept and skipped. Administrators only.

minutes.name: Minutes
minutes.description: Extra time from now, 1 to 1440 minutes. Give this or until.

until.name: Until
until.description: When the extra time ends, instead of minutes (local time without an offset).

cancel_time_bonus.name: Cancel Time Bonus
cancel_time_bonus.description: Cancel extra time on Windows or the Xbox (the Xbox through the Xbox Family Settings API). Only extra time is cancelled: when a lock (ours or a parent's) or nothing is in force, nothing is sent and the answer says so.

account_id.name: Account ID
account_id.description: The user ID of the child account. Give this or an entity of the child.

entity_id.name: Child entity
entity_id.description: Any Microsoft Family Safety entity of the child (or of one of its devices), instead of the account ID.

probe_xapprove.name: Probe Xbox Family Settings API (diagnostic)
probe_xapprove.description: Administrators only. With the Xbox Family Settings sign-in: runs its token steps, looks up the children's Xbox user ids and reads the first child's Xbox override from the Xbox Family Settings API (xapprove), trying a few ways of signing that read until one works; that way is saved and used by the integration. Writes nothing to the Xbox and never uses the Family Safety sign-in. Answers with HTTP status codes, error codes and the override's type and end only; no token, gamertag or Xbox user id is returned or logged. Refuses unless confirm_risk is true: see the README.

entry_id.name: Config entry
entry_id.description: The Microsoft Family Safety entry to use. Optional with a single entry.

confirm_risk.name: Confirm the risk
confirm_risk.description: Must be true. Using the stored sign-in for another scope is not documented by Microsoft for this sign-in type; in the worst case the integration would need a new sign-in.

xbox_schedule_not_restored.title: An Xbox schedule was not put back
xbox_schedule_not_restored.description: An Xbox lock placed through today's Xbox schedule (on {title}) has ended, but its saved day could not be written back yet ({error}). Until it is, that weekday's Xbox daily limit stays at no time. It is retried at every update and this issue goes away once it succeeds. If it persists, check the Xbox schedule in the Family Safety app and set that day back by hand.

xapprove_refused.title: The Xbox Family Settings API refused the Xbox token
xapprove_refused.description:
{title} tried the Xbox Family Settings API (xapprove) and Microsoft refused the Xbox token ({error}). Meanwhile an Xbox lock goes through today's Xbox schedule, and Xbox extra time is not available. xapprove is tried again every 6 hours and this issue goes away once it works.

To fix it, open Settings > Devices & services > Microsoft Family Safety > Configure and tick **Sign in to Xbox Family Settings (next page)** to sign in again with the parent account, or untick **Xbox lock and extra time through the Xbox Family Settings API (xapprove)**. The action microsoft_family_safety.probe_xapprove gives the details.

xbox_signin_expired.title: Sign in to Xbox Family Settings again
xbox_signin_expired.description:
{title} can no longer renew its Xbox Family Settings sign-in: Microsoft refused it (after a password change, a removed app permission, or a long time unused). Meanwhile an Xbox lock goes through today's Xbox schedule, and Xbox extra time is not available.

To fix it, open Settings > Devices & services > Microsoft Family Safety > Configure, tick **Sign in to Xbox Family Settings (next page)**, submit, and follow that page with the parent account. This issue goes away as soon as the new sign-in is saved.
